name: @melra/cli

tools.name: melra_capabilities
tools.description: Discover available local execution capabilities, policy defaults, and runtime limits.

tools.name: melra_plan
tools.description: Persist a bounded task, evaluate policy, and return any scoped approval challenge without executing. Nothing runs until melra_execute. A policy denial comes back as a normal result with status policy_blocked and a reason, not as an error. Any operation that is not a read needs requiredEvidence, and constraints must stay empty.

goal.description: Why this task is being run, in one human-readable sentence.

constraints.description: Leave empty. Freeform prose cannot be enforced, so a non-empty array is denied with freeform_constraints_not_enforceable. Express real limits as forbiddenEffects, budget, or requiredEvidence.

forbiddenEffects.description: Effects this task must never take. Denied before the adapter runs, and honoured even in unhinged mode.

requiredEvidence.description: Predicates that must hold after execution for the task to be verified_success. Required for any non-read operation: a mutation with none is denied with mutation_requires_evidence. An adapter that succeeded while a predicate failed is partial, never success.

reconciliation.description: How to settle this effect if MELRA never learns whether it happened — a request that went out and was never answered, or a crash mid-flight. Read against the facts that were true before the call (idempotencyKey, url, method), never against a response, because there is none. Declaring these makes the executionGuarantee reconciliation-required instead of at-most-once.

identity.description: Who is asking, and on whose behalf. Recorded on the task and every receipt, and matched against policy.capabilities when the operator has issued grants. Omitted means the implicit local principal.

tools.name: melra_execute
tools.description: Execute one previously planned task through policy, runtime, verification, and receipt generation. If melra_plan returned an approval challenge, pass its id and its exact phrase; the phrase is scoped to that one task and expires. Policy is re-evaluated here, so a plan made under a looser policy is still refused. Only reads are retried.

tools.name: melra_task_status
tools.description: Read the current durable state of a task.

tools.name: melra_task_cancel
tools.description: Cooperatively cancel a running or pending task.

tools.name: melra_receipt
tools.description: Retrieve action receipts and the execution certificate.

tools.name: melra_workflow_plan
tools.description: Validate, preflight, encrypt, and persist a bounded workflow without executing it.

tools.name: melra_workflow_advance
tools.description: Execute one ready workflow scheduling wave through governed MELRA tasks.

tools.name: melra_workflow_status
tools.description: Read the current durable workflow projection.

tools.name: melra_workflow_cancel
tools.description: Cooperatively cancel nonterminal workflow nodes and their tasks.

tools.name: melra_workflow_control
tools.description: Halt a running workflow without losing node state, or lift a halt. Node progress is untouched, so a resumed workflow continues where it stopped.

instructions:
MELRA runs effects for you under policy: files, terminal, browser, HTTP, desktop, and memory. Use its tools instead of acting directly, and treat its results as the record of what happened.
For each action:
1. melra_capabilities (once): the operations available and the policy in force: allowed commands and domains, and whether mutations need approval.
2. melra_plan with a goal, one operation, and requiredEvidence. Nothing runs yet. status policy_blocked means refused: read the reason and change the request; the same request will be refused again. status awaiting_approval returns an approval challenge.
3. melra_execute with the taskId, plus the challenge id and its exact phrase if one was issued. Policy is checked again here.
4. Read the status. verified_success means the operation ran and every requiredEvidence check passed. partial means it ran but evidence did not hold. recovery_required means a change may or may not have happened: inspect the world before trying again, never re-run blindly. Only reads are retried for you.
5. melra_receipt returns the receipt and certificate when you need to show what was done.
Rules: any operation that is not a read must declare requiredEvidence describing how to confirm it (result_equals, result_contains, exit_code, file_exists, file_absent, file_hash, page_contains, url_matches, http_resource_matches, custom). custom takes a verifier name from customEvidence in melra_capabilities. Leave constraints empty; free-text constraints are refused because they cannot be enforced.
For multi-step jobs that must survive restarts, use melra_workflow_plan and melra_workflow_advance; each step still goes through the same policy, approval, and verification.
